judgements.justification: B's area chair adopted Reviewer_Xcrv's and Reviewer_t3bd's concerns at a mean of 5.75, not a reading of its own; A's chair followed the scores.
Neither committee rested its recommendation on a forecast of broad impact.
The tightness argument raised A's Reviewer_gM3z to 7; no score in B moved after the rebuttal.
Both committees had thin reviews (A: gM3z, T7tc; B: fudr, AWCx), and B's decisive critic Xcrv read the paper closely, so neither side rests on clearly less scrutiny.
Only B raised the missing comparison with an i.i.d. N-sample, which has a better expected rate and which the authors conceded, and the barycenter cost; both fed B's reject.
Both saw the gap to N^(-2/d), the weak Theorem 7, 2D-only experiments and the need for the density; A took them as future work, B's chair as 'important aspects that are not treated'.
No score changed through reviewer discussion; t3bd cited other reviewers' issues but stayed at 6.
Each rating matches its review's verdict; t3bd's 6 fits 'close to being ready for publication'.
Only AWCx (confidence 2) was unsure, and its 5 rests on stated criticisms, not a declared inability to judge.
No outlier in B; the chair drew on two reviewers, Xcrv and t3bd.
The verbal assessments differ: B's critics raised the i.i.d. baseline and cost, which A never raised.
A's spotlight rests on ratings of 9 and 8 from detailed reviewers, not on agreement alone.
gM3z rose on the tightness result already in the paper (Remark 3, Appendix E), not on unverified rebuttal material.
A's two-sentence meta-review says all reviewers praised 'strong theoretical and numerical contributions' and drops T7tc's 'quite poor' experiments and gM3z's request for d >= 3.
T7tc's misreading of eq. (15) did not move its 6, and no wrong claim about the results fed either recommendation.
The concession about i.i.d. sampling went to B, which rejected; it did not leave a committee higher than its information supported.
Xcrv's late uncited-experiments point went unanswered, but B's meta-review does not rest on it.
The scores differ (mean 7.5 against 5.75), so the split is not a cut-off difference on near-identical reviews.
B's chair followed its confidence-4 critics, and A's most confident reviewer (T7tc) misread the paper; no expert verdict was passed over.
A's concerns (proof slips, tightness) were answerable and lifted gM3z; B's (no i.i.d. baseline, cost, practical value) were about scope, and the response could only concede them.
Neither committee has an outlying score.
No outlying reviewer.
A had no detractor to set aside.
Neither committee raised audience or venue fit.
A's meta-review states that all reviewers stressed strong numerical contributions, while T7tc called the experiments 'quite poor'.
In B, Xcrv replied and t3bd posted a post-rebuttal note; only two of four were silent, and the response conceded rather than answered their points.
No A reviewer said it could not verify the results; the accept scores come from reviewers who checked the proofs.
B split two above (6, 7) and two below (5, 5) at similar confidence; the chair adopted the critics' concerns and did not weigh fudr's 7 or t3bd's 'close to being ready'.
The responses do not conflict; B received a concession only because only B asked.
Both committees agreed the main result is new; no novelty verdict rested on wrong prior work.
A's spotlight has a 9 and an 8 from detailed reviewers behind it, so its scores support the tier even though the meta-review gives no grounds.
B's critics objected to practical significance against a sampling baseline, not to the paper's framing or definitions.

added.name: Only one committee had an engaged champion
added.definition: One committee had reviewers who studied the paper closely and rated it well above the accept level, while the other committee's most positive reviewer gave a light review and did not engage after the rebuttal, so nobody there argued for the paper against its critics.
added.justification: R04 is about scrutiny behind scores and R21 about a single outlying score; neither names the absence of any advocate on one side. Here A's ratings are not outlying, yet two proof-checking champions carried A to a spotlight while B's only 7 came from a reviewer who never engaged, leaving B's chair to hear the critics alone.

reasoning: Both committees found the main result new and correct. B raised a correct point A never saw, the i.i.d.-sample baseline with a better rate, plus the barycenter cost (R05), and weighted the shared practicality gaps more heavily (R06). The rebuttal could answer A's proof-level concerns and lifted gM3z, but could only concede B's scope concerns (R03, R20). B's chair settled a two-two split for the critics (R28). A's meta-review misreported the reviewers' view of the experiments (R14, R25). One new reason covers the champion asymmetry: A had two invested advocates, B had none.
